cells.remarks: Begins with a genealogical account of the king whose descent is traced from Nalla Bhīma of the solar race and Kaśyapa- gōtra. Registers the gift, by the king, to several Brāhmaṇas of the village of Pentapāḍu with two hamlets renamed Gaṅgādharapura. The king is stated to have been installed by Prōlaya Nāyu, son on Vōchana Nāyaka, as governor over this territory. Vōchana, son of Erramaṭi Bhīma, met his later's death in battle against the Muslims. This territory is stated to have been conquest of Chintapanta, Vēngi and Gouṇtūru included in Chintalapūni. Further the gift of the village is stated to have been made by Bhaktirāja after obtaining the consent of Vīra Vōbi Nāyaka, son of Prōlaya Nāyaka.

cells.date: Śaka 994, Paridhāvi, Kārttika, śu. 7, Sunday, saṅkrānti, Vyaṭipāta = A. D. 1072, October 21, Sunday.
cells.remarks: Refers to an interesting dispute about the gaṇḍike (office) of Bēḍage between two parties of Hommaruḷi, each claiming the gaṇḍike for itself. A committee representing prominent persons from several villages round about, met in the temple of god Hanumān at Bēḍage and decided about the gaṇḍike in favour of one party and took the signature of the other party that it would abide by this decision.
